purpose: Primary PostgreSQL 17 mechanisms; no Core schema/producer or runtime qualification.

inspected_points: Policies restrict rows independently of the application working-state field. Superusers/BYPASSRLS and ordinarily table owners bypass policies.
Referential integrity checks bypass RLS and can create covert channels; an identity constraint is not permission to reveal a protected match.
Policy subqueries consulting mutable authorization rows can race; the documented locking discussion supports testing an explicit cooperating authority fence.
An updater or SELECT FOR UPDATE/SHARE waits for a conflicting updater. After commit, its search condition is re-evaluated against the updated row.
The fixture uses explicit current authority/source locks and revision checks; the tests observe real waits rather than assuming an earlier read remains current.
A partial index contains only rows satisfying its predicate. A partial unique index constrains that subset without constraining the other rows.
A uniqueness predicate limited to active records can permit another canonical-key row while the original is archived.
A unique multicolumn index rejects rows only when all indexed columns compare equal. NULLs are distinct by default.
Fixture tenant/canonical_key columns are NOT NULL and constrained across both states. The key is a synthetic resolved identity, not email or a product matching rule.
